claims.statement: Mark Granovetter published The Strength of Weak Ties in AJS 78(6), May 1973, pages 1360-1380
claims.locator: Original scanned journal p1360; publisher metadata

claims.statement: The 1973 article frames interpersonal network analysis as micro-to-macro sociological linkage
Tie strength conceptualized using time, emotional intensity, intimacy, reciprocal services; relationships assumed positive and symmetric for essay
Strong ties tend to involve more neighborhood overlap; the missing B-C tie despite strong A-B and A-C is treated as improbable, idealized as absent in a thought argument
claims.locator: pp1362-1363 forbidden triad and explicit exaggeration

claims.statement: Bridge vs local bridge; a local bridge's endpoints have alternate shortest path longer than two when that edge is removed
claims.locator: pp1364-1365 original Fig2 and local bridge degree

claims.statement: Weak ties are not necessarily local bridges; claim that no strong tie is a bridge needs structural assumptions
1973 paper reports N=54 contact-mediated job changers: 16.7% frequent, 55.6% occasional, 27.8% rare contact
1973 footnote: N54 arises from in-person subsample of 100 out of 282; contact frequency proxy is not full tie-strength measure
1973 paper considers weak-tie abundance as alternative to special bridge function, lacking baseline population contact frequencies
Getting a Job is a separate 1974 volume and 1983 revisited article not identical to 1973 paper
A-C-D-E-B local bridge example and two triangles joined by one edge are author-invented teaching networks, not archival study participants
